name: Boning
summary: A way to stiffen a bodice with thin strips of whalebone, cane or steel set in narrow channels, so that the cloth holds the shape of the torso.
how: Sew two or three layers of strong cloth together.
Stitch narrow channels, 6 to 10 mm wide, from the waist to the chest.
Push one strip of bone or steel into each channel and close the end.
Bind each edge of the garment in leather or tape.

origin.note: Boned bodices of linen and whalebone appear at the courts of Europe.

adoptions.via: Stay-makers cut linen stays with whalebone strips in sewn channels and shaped them into a cone.
Steel boning became popular and gave the corset a bone that springs back.
Designers put the boned bodice on the street as a top and a dress.
